# Delivery Handbook

This preamble introduces the handbook and explains how the budget sections fit together for every delivery team that plans its work here.

## Budget planning

Budget planning starts each quarter. The budget owner collects the estimates, and the budget is confirmed at the planning review. Every work item carries a budget line from the first estimate onward.

## Budget approval

Budget approval happens after the estimates are signed. The budget approval meeting records who approved the budget and which exceptions were granted for the quarter.

## Budget tracking

Budget tracking runs monthly. The tracking report compares the spent amount with the budget plan and flags every budget overrun for the next review.

## Budget revisions

A budget revision is needed when scope moves. The revision request names the budget lines that change and the reason, and the budget owner signs it before the work continues.

## Budget reporting

Budget reporting summarises the quarter. The report lists the budget per work item, the spent share, and the forecast for the next budget period.

## Budget retrospective

The budget retrospective closes the cycle. The team reviews which budget assumptions held, which budget lines drifted, and what the next budget cycle should change.

## Release checklist

The release checklist does not mention money at all; it lists the steps a release needs, from the build to the announcement and the documentation update.
